To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

PapD, a periplasmic bacterial chaperone, binds extended beta-strands of peptides in aqueous solution and that the peptide binds to PapD through backbone to backbone hydrogen bonding and hydrophobic interactions.
peptides derived from the C-terminal region of the adhesin of P-fimbriae bind to the periplasmic PapD chaperone in aqueous solution, forming an extended, beta-sheet like structure.

peptides derived from the adhesin of the PapG pilus of uropathogenic Escherichia coil bind to PapD, the chaperone for PapG, in solution and that this binding involves backbone to backbone hydrogen bonding and hydrophobic interactions.
